To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) insulin loaded mucoadhesives nanoparticles (NPs), based on mucin and chitosan, were prepared and characterized, (2) insulin loaded NPs exhibited a sustained release profile in vitro, (3) the prepared NPs were biocompatible and showed low toxicity, and (4) insulin loaded NPS showed a pronounced hypoglyaemic activity in diabetic rats after a peroral administration.

insulin loaded NPs prepared by self gelation method of chitosan and mucin showed promising results in terms of particle size and morphology, encapsulation efficiency, release kinetics, pharmacokinetic and in vivo antidiabetic activity in diabetic rats.
insulin-loaded nanoparticles were successfully prepared via self-gelation method and the prepared nanoparticles showed good stability in gastric and intestinal fluids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new oral insulin delivery system that is safe for use, and that can potentially replace the currently used subcutaneous injection of insulin.
the development of a novel oral insulin delivery system based on chitosan and mucin.
the design, synthesis and characterization of novel chitosan and mucins based NPs for oral insulin delivery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the insulin loaded chitosan snail mucin NPs are a promising approach for oral insulin delivery.

this work has demonstrated a promising and novel approach to protect insulin from degradation in acidic gastric environment and to increase the oral absorption of the peptide hormone by the formation of chitosan-mucin nanoparticles.
insulin loaded chitosan snail mucin nanoparticles are promising for oral insulin delivery and diabetes management.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prepared NPs of insulin could potentially be used for oral delivery and treatment of diabetes.
the prepared NPs of insulin could be considered as a promising approach for the oral delivery of insulin.
we have prepared a new insulin delivery system based on natural polymers (chitosan and snails mucin) which is able to enhance the peroral delivery of the protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chitosan and mucin can be used to formulate insulin loaded NPs for peroral delivery of insulin and diabetes treatment.
the use of chitosan/mucin NPs as a delivery system for oral administration of insulin can improve the stability and bioavailability of insulin.
the combination of chitosan and soluble mucin is an effective strategy to develop insulin loaded NPs for oral delivery.
